Once you have added this application, you need to add a `.clabot` file to your repository, which provides details of contributors who have a signed CLA.

Full installation instructions can be [found on the project website](https://colineberhardt.github.io/cla-bot/#installing-cla-bot).

Three review-feedback fixes (squashed into the existing commit):

**(1) Ordering by `(occurred_at, id)` again.** The id-only cursor assumed UUID byte-order ≈ event time, but `id` is wall-clock at *mint* time and drifts from `occurred_at` when callers pre-set `event.id()`, when ring slots sit before the sink runs, or when bulkImport carries through original ids. Restored the composite cursor used pre-migration across SQLite / MySQL / Postgres / Mongo / InMemory. Id stays as the tiebreaker for same-ms bursts.

**(2) Redis pagination tracks `(score, member)` on the cursor.** Previous exclusive lower bound `(X` skipped every other member at score `X`. Now inclusive lower bound + in-client skip-past-cursor restores `(occurred_at, id)` lex ordering at boundaries. No data loss mid-burst.

**(3) SQL migrations are crash-safe.**
- MySQL: atomic multi-table `RENAME TABLE old TO backup, new TO old` (single statement — neither rename happens if either fails). On next-boot, if `oldTable` already has `BINARY(16)` ids (swap done, schema_version commit didn't), skip rewrite and drop the leftover backup.
- Postgres & SQLite: wrap the whole create / copy / swap in a single transaction. Crash anywhere before `COMMIT` rolls back to the pre-migration shape with the canonical data untouched.

The three failure modes from the review — `DROP IF EXISTS new_temp` killing the only copy after a swap-side crash, `DROP old` then separate `RENAME new TO old` opening a crash window, and `DROP IF EXISTS` ahead of an old-table existence check — are all gone.

Sorry — my earlier rebase with `--autosquash --root` rewrote committer dates on every commit between origin/master and my fix, which made the PR show ~80 commits. The branch content was unchanged but the SHAs were all new, so GitHub treated them as new commits.

Branch is now reset to exactly one commit on top of origin/master with just the UUIDv7 fix. Same content, clean diff.
